newsitem.title: UK: Pay up, German official tells EBRD members.
newsitem.headline: Pay up, German official tells EBRD members.

text.p: Senior German finance ministry official Juergen Stark on Monday hit out at member nations of the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development who have yet to pay up to allow the Bank to double its capital. Germany, despite its own "severe" budgetary problems, had stuck to its word and paid its share of the extra financing early this year, Stark, state secretary at the finance ministry, said at the Bank's annual meeting.

"I regret one third of the subscriptions have yet to be undertaken," Stark told the EBRD's annual conference in London. "I trust that all other members of the Bank will fulfil their commitments without delay."
The EBRD's annual meeting in Sofia last year agreed to double the Bank's capital. EBRD members and management had agreed that there will be no further capital increase, Stark said.
"The Bank must from now on finance the envisaged expansion of its operations from repayments and profits," he said.
The EBRD last year agreed to double its subscribed capital to 20 billion ecu. -- Mike Peacock, London Newsroom +44 171 542 5109
